items.claim: [r38-5] A coast canceled from outside leaves its preview on screen and records nothing (carried, B)
items.note: It is contradicted by `docs/unruled.md`, under "Audit round six (2026-11-08)". That entry describes exactly this case: a coast over an adapter with `previewPoses` and no pose targets, canceled by `cancelAll` or by the animator going away. It says the coast "leaves its last frame as a preview and records nothing, as the code says it means to. Left as is: it could record where the coast stopped, or clear the preview." The code still matches that entry. When `coast.stop` in `coastByWrite.ts:41-50` finds the decay no longer active, it only removes the coast from the set. It never reaches `commitFlick`, so no flick op is written and the preview is not cleared. The other path the finding cites, a coast on pose targets (`coastOnTargets.ts:166-170`), is not affected. There, `animator.watch` sees the cancel and halts each node, and `commitFlick` then records the flick. Choosing between recording the stop and clearing the preview is still the open decision that entry names.

items.claim: Coast canceled from outside (`cancelAll`, `cancelKey`, unmount) records nothing; over pose targets it moves the document outside history
items.note: This is the fixer's call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`: on every adapter the coast now records the flick where it stopped and clears its preview. That replaces round six's "left as is" entry for the `previewPoses` path, which B's report also covers.

items.claim: `scenePoseTarget` returns a stale target for a node deleted at rest, and its cache grows without bound
items.note: A lookup now drops that target, and making a new one sweeps the dead ones out each time the table doubles.

items.claim: Rewinding tween with an easing that overshoots ends early and jumps
`rigFromNode` loses the skin of a node whose id is `__proto__`
`useRigNode` throws during render on a joint the skeleton no longer has
items.note: This is the fixer's call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`: such joints are left out and `useRigNode` warns about them; `bindRig` still throws on one.

items.claim: `Rig.bake` throws, and `show` puts an override back each frame, for a bound or skinned node deleted after binding
items.note: B also said a node locked since binding throws: not a defect (refusing a write to a locked node is what a lock does).

items.claim: `boundary: 'stop'` behaves differently on pose targets than through writes
items.note: Each node now stops at its own edge on both paths.

items.claim: `momentum({ friction: 1 })` throws at release on one adapter and coasts forever on the other
items.note: This is the fixer's call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`: `momentum()` throws a `RangeError` on a friction outside (0, 1).

items.claim: `rig.bake()` throws once a bound or skinned node is deleted
`useRigNode` / `rigFromNode` lose the skin of a `__proto__` node id
`scenePoseTarget` keeps, and hands back, the target of a node deleted while at rest, and its cache grows without bound
items.note: A lookup now drops the stale target, and the table clears out at-rest targets of deleted nodes each time it doubles. No test covers the clearing on its own, because the table's size can't be seen from outside.

items.claim: `animateLifecycle` gets stuck in `leaving`, or leaves the node at its enter pose, when `tweenPose` throws
items.note: This needed a behavior call, which is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`: the error still throws, the inserted node is left at its own pose, and the node can be removed again.

items.claim: `animateLifecycle` removes a node that is inserted again while its exit animation runs

items.note: They now follow round nineteen's ruling and share one `defaultMotionMs` with the reflow glide. A `spring` option still springs, and that call is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: `momentum`'s `boundary: 'stop'` lets a node slide along an edge over an adapter with no pose targets
`momentum`'s pose-target coast writes the document with no history entry after an outside cancel
items.note: This needed a behavior call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`: the flick is recorded where it stopped, as one undo step. Round six's line on the `previewPoses` path stands. The editing test's stub animator gained a `watch` method.

items.claim: A rewinding tween ends a leg early under an easing that overshoots
A skinned node with a rotated pose gets its rotation applied twice when baked
items.note: `PoseDescriptor.fromBounds` is documented to carry none of the template's shape, and every kit descriptor drops rotation there. The existing test "skins a turned node from where it is drawn, and shows it with no turn left to apply" covers this case.
